key_insight: Uncertainty-guided simulation enrichment improves neural-network surrogates for microdroplet generation and supports confidence-aware inverse design.
engineering_relevance: The framework reduces reliance on costly multiphase-flow simulations when designing microfluidic devices for target droplet sizes.
method: Train neural-network ensembles on high-fidelity Volume-of-Fluid simulations to predict flow regimes and droplet diameters.
Use regime consensus and diameter coefficient of variation to target additional simulations near uncertain transitions and address class imbalance.
Apply Particle Swarm Optimization for constrained inverse design, balancing target accuracy, predictive confidence, and physical consistency.
evidence_signal: On independent test datasets, enrichment nearly doubled the fraction of diameter predictions with 0–3% error and substantially reduced cases above 10% error.
watch_item: Ensemble agreement does not guarantee accuracy outside the simulated parameter space; new operating conditions may require additional high-fidelity validation.
paper_title: Microdroplet Generator Surrogate Enhancement and Inverse Design Through an Uncertainty-Guided Framework
